title: What qualifications, training and CPD do UAE insurance brokers and agents need under Central Bank rules?
seoTitle: CBUAE insurance broker and agent rules
description: Central Bank of the UAE rules on insurance broker and agent competence: fit and proper criteria, training courses, exams, 15 CPD hours and specialised staff.
shortAnswer: The Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) requires insurance brokers to meet fit and proper criteria under its Insurance Brokers' Regulation, in force from February 15, 2025, including minimum qualifications and experience for senior managers and specialised employees and 15 hours of continuing professional development each year, evidenced at license renewal. Individual insurance agents must hold an insurance diploma, two years' experience, attend prescribed training courses and pass examinations under Insurance Authority Board Resolution No. 08 of 2011.
keyTakeaways: The CBUAE Insurance Brokers' Regulation (C 1/2024) took effect on February 15, 2025 and replaced the 2013 Insurance Authority brokerage regulation as the main rulebook for brokers.
Article 5.6 requires a broker's annual license renewal to include proof that its representatives, senior management and specialised employees completed 15 hours of CPD.

A broker's chief executive needs a bachelor's degree or ACII (or equivalent advanced diploma), three completed insurance or brokerage training courses, and ten years' experience (five for a UAE national).
Every broker must have at least one CBUAE approved specialised employee for each licensed line of business, with a bachelor's degree and five years' experience (three for a UAE national).
Natural person insurance agents must be UAE nationals with a secondary certificate and an insurance diploma, two years' insurer experience, prescribed training courses and a pass in the examinations.
jurisdiction: United Arab Emirates (federal; onshore insurance market)
regulator: Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), which took over the functions of the former Insurance Authority
appliesTo: Insurance brokers licensed by the CBUAE, including branches of foreign brokers, and their representatives, senior management, specialised employees and staff
Natural person and corporate insurance agents registered in the Insurance Agents Register, excluding agents in free zones with their own rules
Insurance companies that contract with agents and deal with brokers

sections.heading: Which CBUAE rules set competence requirements for brokers and agents?

blocks.text: Two instruments do most of the work. For brokers, the [CBUAE Insurance Brokers' Regulation](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/insurance-brokers%E2%80%99-regulation), reference C 1/2024, shown in the CBUAE Rulebook as effective from February 15, 2025 and in force as at November 2026. It was issued under Decretal Federal Law No. (14) of 2018 on the Central Bank and Decretal Federal Law No. (48) of 2023 Concerning the Organization of Insurance Operations, and its preamble lists Insurance Authority Board Resolution No. (15) of 2013 on insurance brokerage among the instruments it builds on.

For agents, the governing text remains [Insurance Authority Board Resolution No. 08 of 2011 Instructions Concerning the Regulation of Insurance Agents Business](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/insurance-authority-board-resolution-no-08-2011-instructions-concerning-regulation), effective April 28, 2011 and still marked "In-Force" in the CBUAE Rulebook. It applies to all insurance agents in the UAE except those operating in free zones under their own laws (Article 2).

A third category, insurance producers who market policies through ordinary or electronic means, is licensed under Insurance Authority Board of Directors' Resolution No. (27) of 2020, effective November 18, 2020. This page focuses on brokers and agents.

sections.heading: What qualifications and experience must broker managers and specialists have?

blocks.text: Brokers must put every key individual through a fit and proper process covering qualifications, knowledge, experience, integrity and a CBUAE assessment. [Article 5.1](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/article-5-fit-and-propper-process) lists the criteria, including "meeting the necessary qualifications, knowledge and experience requirements" and "passing the assessment determined by the Central Bank for this purpose". Article 5.3 and 5.4 then set minimums by role:

blocks.text: Academic degrees must be accredited as equivalent by the competent UAE authority (Article 5.5), and the CBUAE may exempt nominees from conditions case by case (Article 5.8). Article 5.7 requires representatives, senior management, specialised employees and staff to meet the fit and proper requirements "on an on-going basis", so competence is not a one time hiring check.

sections.heading: How much CPD must broker staff complete, and how is it evidenced?

blocks.text: Fifteen hours a year, evidenced with the annual license renewal. Article 5.6 requires a broker to submit, with its renewal application, "an annual report... that contains proof of completion of fifteen (15) hours of continuing professional development for the Insurance Broker's Representatives, Senior Management and Specialised Employees". It defines CPD as including insurance or brokerage conferences, training programs and workshops.

The timing is set by Article 2.16: a broker's license lasts one year and must be renewed at least one month before it expires, and the CBUAE may revoke the license if the broker fails to do so. In practice the CPD year should close in time to compile the report before that deadline.

Staffing rules in [Article 4](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/article-4-going-requirements) reinforce competence. A broker must have "adequate Staff who possess the requisite qualifications, competencies and skills" for every licensed line, and at least one specialised employee for each licensed insurance type at all times. It must notify the CBUAE of appointments, transfers and terminations of specialised employees, and fill a vacancy with an alternative within 30 days.

blocks.title: Who counts as a specialised employee?
blocks.text: Article 1.35 defines a specialised employee as an employee appointed by the broker and approved by the Central Bank to conduct core insurance brokerage activities in specific lines of business, based on qualifications and experience. Representatives (Article 1.19) are the partners or board, and staff (Article 1.36) means everyone working for the broker other than the representatives.

sections.heading: What training and examinations must insurance agents complete?

blocks.text: A natural person agent must combine formal insurance education, experience, prescribed training and an examination. [Article 6 of Resolution No. 08 of 2011](https://rulebook.centralbank.ae/en/rulebook/article-6-conditions-registration) requires the applicant to:

items: be a UAE national, aged at least 21, with full legal capacity
hold a secondary education certificate and "a diploma in insurance from an institute recognized by the IA, as a minimum"
have at least two years' practical experience in insurance business with an insurance company
"have attended the training courses as determined by a decision of the Director General"
practice full time, be of good conduct, and have no prior suspension or cancellation for disciplinary reasons in any insurance related profession
"successfully pass the examinations at the IA"

blocks.text: A corporate agent needs paid up capital of at least AED 500,000, generally owned by UAE nationals, and its manager in charge must meet the natural person conditions except nationality. Article 3 adds that an agent may act for only one insurance company and must hold an agency contract filed with the regulator. Under Article 12, renewal requires an application at least one month before the registration term expires, and corporate agents must list all key staff in charge of agency business.

Agents' references to "the IA" now point to the CBUAE, which administers the resolution through its Rulebook. Confirm with the CBUAE which examinations and Director General training decisions currently apply, because the resolution delegates their content.

sections.heading: What competence evidence should a broker or agent keep?

blocks.text: The CBUAE can request any data at any time (Article 4.5(f) of the brokers' regulation), so each competence requirement needs a current record. sections.heading: How does the UAE compare with other insurance distribution regimes?

blocks.text: The EU Insurance Distribution Directive also sets an annual CPD minimum for distributors, but the UAE's 15 hour rule attaches to named senior roles and specialised employees and is evidenced at company level through license renewal. US states license individual producers and set their own continuing education hours. See [Insurance Distribution Directive CPD requirements](/regulations/insurance-distribution-directive-cpd-requirements), [US insurance producer continuing education](/regulations/insurance-producer-continuing-education-requirements) and the cross market summary in [financial services competence requirements by country](/compare/financial-services-competence-requirements-by-country).

Insurers and brokers also face separate CBUAE conduct obligations; see [UAE Central Bank consumer protection training](/regulations/uae-central-bank-consumer-protection-training). For the wider sector context, see the [financial services industry page](/industries/financial-services).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry models each fit and proper criterion, CPD rule and agent registration condition as an obligation tied to a named role and its evidence, so a broker can see before renewal which individuals are short of their 15 hours and which lines lack an approved specialised employee.

faqs.q: When did the CBUAE Insurance Brokers' Regulation take effect?
faqs.a: The CBUAE Rulebook shows the regulation (C 1/2024) as effective from February 15, 2025. Article 23 says it came into effect six months after publication in the Official Gazette and required brokers and insurers to regularize their status before that date.

faqs.q: Who must complete the 15 hours of CPD at a UAE insurance broker?
faqs.a: Article 5.6 names the broker's representatives (partners or board), senior management and specialised employees. Proof of completion goes in an annual report submitted with the license renewal application. Other staff are not named in the 15 hour rule, but must meet fit and proper requirements on an ongoing basis.

faqs.q: Can a non UAE national register as an individual insurance agent?
faqs.a: Not as a natural person. Article 6 of Resolution No. 08 of 2011 requires a natural person agent to be a UAE national. A corporate agent's manager in charge must meet the other natural person conditions, but the nationality condition does not apply to that manager.

faqs.q: Does ACII satisfy the broker CEO qualification?
faqs.a: Yes, as one route. Article 5.3 accepts a bachelor's degree, the ACII designation from the Chartered Insurance Institute, or an advanced diploma from a similar accredited professional institute, combined with three insurance training courses and the required years of experience.
